title: Career Roadmap: Trading Analyst
summary: A Trading Analyst analyzes financial markets, price movements, trading activity, risk exposures and quantitative indicators to support trading decisions. Depending on the employer, the role may involve equities, derivatives, currencies, commodities, fixed income or algorithmic trading.

blocks.text: For students studying quantitative finance or financial mathematics, this career combines probability, statistics, mathematical modeling, programming and financial-market knowledge.

rows.text: Analyze market data and support trading decisions and execution

Banks, brokerage firms, proprietary trading firms, asset managers and fintech companies

blocks.label: Important distinction
blocks.text: A Trading Analyst supports analysis, execution or monitoring, depending on the desk. A Quantitative Researcher primarily develops and tests mathematical trading models, while a Trader may make or execute trading decisions within defined risk limits. Some firms combine these responsibilities.

blocks.label: Beginner stack
blocks.text: Python + pandas + Jupyter + SQL + Excel + a documented historical market dataset. Start with research and simulated trading before considering live execution.
Use public or properly licensed historical datasets. Document assumptions, and treat results as research rather than evidence of guaranteed future returns.
Project 1 — Market Returns and Volatility Analyzer
Beginner
Analyze historical prices for selected instruments and calculate returns, rolling volatility, correlations and maximum drawdown.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Python notebook, charts and a concise findings report.
Project 2 — Rule-Based Strategy Backtest
Intermediate
Test a simple, predefined trading rule on historical data. Compare it with a benchmark and include fees, slippage assumptions and out-of-sample testing.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Reproducible backtest, benchmark comparison and limitations report.
Project 3 — Portfolio Risk and Performance Dashboard
Intermediate
Measure portfolio returns, volatility, correlation, drawdowns and risk-adjusted performance under different market conditions.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Interactive dashboard with documented assumptions and risk metrics.
Project 4 — Quantitative Trading Research Framework
Advanced
Build a research pipeline that imports data, validates its quality, creates features, tests a hypothesis, evaluates out-of-sample performance and produces a risk report.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Modular code, experiment log, benchmark results and a research paper-style report.

blocks.label: Portfolio standards
blocks.text: Avoid look-ahead bias, data leakage and overfitting. Separate training and test periods, include realistic trading costs, and explain why a historical result may not persist in future markets. Do not publish private trading data or credentials.
Look for internships involving quantitative analysis, trading support, market research, risk analytics or financial data engineering.

blocks.label: Recommendation
blocks.text: If you want to become a quantitative researcher at a mathematically intensive firm, prioritize advanced probability, statistics, linear algebra and programming. A postgraduate degree may help, but the best route depends on the employer's hiring criteria.

blocks.label: Recommended priority
blocks.text: Start with probability, statistics and Python. Then learn financial-market fundamentals, analyze historical data and build a carefully tested backtesting project. Apply for Trading Analyst, Quantitative Research Intern, Trading Operations and Market Risk roles based on your strengths.
For this career, mathematical depth + programming ability + rigorous research habits are more valuable than simply learning technical chart patterns or attempting to trade with real money.
